name: Thurn
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village above Lienz, offering stunning views of the town and the surrounding mountains.
beschreibung:
Overview

Thurn is perched at an elevation of 855 meters on a sunny, fog-free terrace north of the town of Lienz in East Tyrol. Together with its neighbor villages Gaimberg and Oberlienz, the settlement forms part of the acclaimed 'Lienz Sun Villages', famous for enjoying some of Austria's highest sunshine hours. Home to approximately 630 residents, this peaceful farming community stretches from roughly 720 meters near the valley floor up to the Rotgföllschneid at 2,738 meters in the Schober Group of the Hohe Tauern National Park. Revered as the 'Balcony of Lienz', Thurn offers sweeping, unobstructed views across the entire Lienz basin toward the jagged limestone battlements of the Lienz Dolomites, including the Spitzkofel, Laserzwand, and Rauchkofel.

History

The settlement was first documented in 1308. Its name originates from the Middle High German word for tower ('Thurn'), reflecting two historical defensive strongholds: a medieval residential tower on the Schlößlbichl in the Großbachtal ravine and the later noble residence of Castle Thurn near the village church. A remarkable jewel of regional vernacular architecture is the heritage-listed Kammerlanderhof in the upper hamlet of Oberdorf. First mentioned in 1545, with core timbers dating to around 1500, the farmstead remained virtually unchanged across four centuries before being carefully restored by the municipality and local cultural association. Today it functions as an authentic living farm museum, showcasing an original soot-blackened smokehouse kitchen (Rauchküche) with open hearth, traditional timber parlors, and a massive grain granary. The parish church of Saint Nicholas features 12th-century Romanesque origins, was enlarged in Gothic style in 1416, and received an ornate Baroque high altar in 1696, serving also as a regional pilgrimage site.

Getting There

By car, Thurn is accessed from Salzburg or Munich via the Felbertauern Road B108 to Lienz. Drivers from Carinthia or South Tyrol follow the Drautal Road B100. From Lienz, state road L323 (Lienz-Thurner-Straße) winds up the sunny hillside in merely five minutes. Rail travelers arrive at Lienz Hauptbahnhof along the Drau Valley line. Regular regional bus route 942 runs multiple times daily from Lienz station directly to Thurn village square.

Tips

A guided tour of the Kammerlanderhof museum reveals the authentic realities of early alpine farming life, centered around its ancient smokehouse kitchen and granary. Directly from Thurn, a panoramic mountain road leads up to the Zettersfeld plateau: this sun-drenched mountain offers high-altitude walks along the Zirbenweg stone pine trail and scenic hikes to the Neualpl lakes in summer, turning into a family-oriented ski resort above 1,800 meters during winter. A relaxing stroll along the Thurn panoramic terrace loop delivers unforgettable perspectives of the Lienz Dolomites.
